calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on every load-bearing fact: guidance $89.85-90.95B, consensus ~$90.6-90.7B, FY26 beat history +1.5% to +3.2% vs the guidance midpoint, and the Oct 28 report date. Two factual items cannot be settled without web access: (1) Chartmill's $92.45B consensus against the ~$90.65B consensus from the others, which I treat as stale or differently defined and give little weight; (2) the size of FX headwinds in Jul-Sep 2026, left as added downside width. The one judgment dispute is whether the Q4 3.2% beat persists; I treated it as partly lumpy, put the median at the mean beat (~2.0%, $92.2B), and gave the low tail slightly more weight (p_below 3%) than the runs did, because four quarters is a small sample and FX is unverified. My median lands where the runs did because the shared evidence puts it there, not because I averaged them.
